a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is almotriptan, a triptan with a 3-(2-dimethylaminoethyl)indole core and a 5-(pyrrolidin-1-ylsulfonylmethyl) substituent; L5 retrieves gut-wall transport records for close triptan analogs zolmitriptan and eletriptan and for basic amines.

Zolmitriptan, a close triptan analog, shows bidirectional Caco-2 transport with linear flux over 0.2–10 mM and A-B/B-A ratios ~1.5–2.6, indicating passive diffusion without concentration-dependent efflux saturation; P-gp inhibition increases AP-BL transport but transport remains substantial.

Eletriptan, a triptan with a sulfonyl-containing 5-substituent similar to the query, is absorbed at 32 ± 2.5 µg/h/cm in rat duodenum and 26 ± 6.6 µg/h/cm in jejunum, supporting efficient intestinal uptake for this scaffold.

Imipramine, a basic amine with similar ionization, shows Caco-2 Papp 10.8 × 10^-6 cm/s and essentially 100% absorption; even with a FaSSIF P-gp efflux ratio of 2.0, A-B permeability remains high at 19 × 10^-6 cm/s.
L4 solubility records for zolmitriptan show high aqueous solubility across GI pH (1.70 mg/mL water, 9.79 mg/mL pH 6.8, 20.26 mg/mL pH 1.2), supporting dissolution for the triptan scaffold.

L1 gold contexts are predominantly high absolute F measurements (bepridil 59–62%, vilazodone 72%, flavoxate ~100%, sulthiame complete, 5-HTP 49%); the only low-F context (ilomastat) is structurally unrelated and not transferable.
L5 efflux records for structurally dissimilar low-F compounds (e.g., sulpiride) are not transferable to the query; mechanism alone does not establish F < 20%.
L3 oral exposure records for triptans (zolmitriptan, rizatriptan, eletriptan) show measurable systemic Cmax after oral dosing, confirming oral absorption for the triptan class.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for almotriptan is present in any card.
No matched oral-versus-IV AUC/Cmax comparison is available for the query.
No direct query-specific permeability, solubility, efflux, or intestinal metabolism measurement exists; L3-L5 values come from analogs.
Food effect and first-pass metabolism for the query are unknown.
L5 efflux data are mechanistic and not direct F endpoints.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F >= 20%). No threshold-relevant low-F evidence transfers to the query. Confidence remains moderate because no direct query-specific F measurement exists.
